title: Narrative Voice and Technique
text:
Many classic novels rely on a distinctive narrative voice to shape how readers perceive events. In Jane Austen's works, for example, the narrator often slips into the minds of characters, revealing their private thoughts with gentle irony. This technique, known as free indirect discourse, allows the author to comment on society without stepping outside the story. Readers therefore experience the plot through a filter of personality and judgement.

Writers of the nineteenth century also used symbolism to deepen their themes. A recurring image, such as a storm or a locked door, can suggest a character's inner conflict without any explicit explanation. Careful readers who notice these patterns often find that the text rewards repeated study. For this reason, style and technique are inseparable from the meaning of a novel.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what is the name of the technique in which the narrator reveals characters' private thoughts?
According to paragraph two, what can a recurring image such as a storm suggest?
options: The historical date of the setting

questions.text: What can be inferred about the narrator in Austen's works from paragraph one?
options: It never reveals any character's thoughts
It appears only in the opening chapter
It judges characters with a subtle, ironic tone
It is unrelated to the society of the novel

questions.text: What does the passage suggest about reading classic novels?
options: It should be done only once
It is less rewarding than modern fiction
It depends entirely on the reader's age
Repeated study can reveal deeper meaning

paragraph_translations: Muchas novelas clásicas se basan en una voz narrativa distintiva para dar forma a la manera en que los lectores perciben los acontecimientos. En las obras de Jane Austen, por ejemplo, el narrador a menudo se introduce en la mente de los personajes, revelando sus pensamientos privados con una ironía suave. Esta técnica, conocida como discurso indirecto libre, permite al autor comentar la sociedad sin salir de la historia. Por ello, los lectores experimentan la trama a través de un filtro de personalidad y juicio.

Los escritores del siglo XIX también usaron el simbolismo para profundizar sus temas. Una imagen recurrente, como una tormenta o una puerta cerrada, puede sugerir el conflicto interior de un personaje sin ninguna explicación explícita. Los lectores atentos que notan estos patrones suelen descubrir que el texto recompensa la lectura repetida. Por esta razón, el estilo y la técnica son inseparables del significado de una novela.
